result.summary: The environment features a wide, two-lane roadway with sidewalks on both sides, separated by a small grass buffer in some areas. However, the lack of marked crossings, traffic calming measures, and the presence of multiple driveway curb cuts create a high-speed environment with frequent conflict points for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide, unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The wide road width without traffic calming or marked crossings encourages higher vehicle speeds and makes crossing difficult.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway

hazards.name: Frequent driveway curb cuts
hazards.description: Multiple vehicle access points across the sidewalk increase the risk of pedestrian-vehicle conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side sidewalk

hazards.name: Degraded pavement

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing locations and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or other vertical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds along this residential/commercial stretch.

result.summary: The environment is a residential street with a narrow, degraded sidewalk and significant roadway pavement cracking. Pedestrian safety is compromised by the lack of marked crossings, visual obstructions from large trees and parked cars, and poor infrastructure maintenance.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is heavily cracked and degraded, which can lead to tripping hazards or unpredictable vehicle movements.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface in the foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: A vehicle is parked partially on the sidewalk area, forcing pedestrians into the grass or roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, under the large tree

hazards.name: Lack of crossing infrastructure
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs despite the residential context.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible roadway

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway to eliminate cracks and potholes, improving safety for all users.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks to provide designated crossing points for residents.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Repair and widen the existing sidewalk to meet ADA standards and ensure a clear path of travel.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a marked midblock crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of traffic calming or pedestrian refuge islands create a long, unprotected crossing for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two travel lanes and two parking lanes without a refuge island, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the marked crosswalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the crosswalk edges can block the sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street adjacent to the crosswalk markings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crosswalk to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, continuous sidewalk, but it is interrupted by a large, unmarked driveway/alley entrance that creates a significant conflict zone. The roadway lacks clear lane markings, which may contribute to less predictable vehicle behavior and higher speeds in this residential/mixed-use setting.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Driveway Conflict
hazards.description: A wide driveway/alley entrance crosses the sidewalk without markings or a raised crossing, creating a large area of potential conflict between pedestrians and vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the paved alley meets the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of center lines or lane markings on the roadway can lead to higher vehicle speeds and less predictable positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway.

interventions.title: Raised Driveway Crossing
interventions.description: Maintain the sidewalk level and material across the driveway entrance to signal pedestrian priority and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Roadway Striping
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to define travel lanes, which can help regulate vehicle speeds and positioning.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Install street trees or a planting strip between the curb and sidewalk to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.
